trackers.title: US Measles Tracker
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the 2026 US measles surge: CDC case counts, cases by state, outbreaks, deaths, elimination status and a dated timeline.

status.label: Growing · most since 1991
status.summary: CDC counted 4,080 confirmed cases in 47 jurisdictions as of 8 October, up 193 in a week. Pennsylvania's outbreak, centred on Lancaster County, has passed 1,000 cases and five deaths by the state's count, while CDC counts two deaths. A regional health body will decide in November whether the US has lost the measles elimination status it has held since 2000.

trackers.headline: US measles cases pass 4,000 and reach 4,080, the most since 1991. Pennsylvania's outbreak has passed 1,000 cases and New York has declared a disaster emergency.

trackers.title: Ebola Tracker: DR Congo
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: confirmed cases and deaths, affected provinces, spread to other countries, vaccines, WHO risk and a dated timeline.

status.label: Growing · global health emergency
status.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak declared on 15 May has spread to 64 health zones in 7 of DR Congo's 26 provinces. ECDC, reporting DR Congo's data, counted 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 deaths as of 6 October; CDC calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. There is no licensed vaccine for this strain; trials of an existing Ebola vaccine began in August, and an early-phase trial of a Bundibugyo-specific candidate began in Uganda on 6 October.

trackers.headline: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 8,700 confirmed cases and 4,200 deaths. Kenya reports its first imported case.

latest.title: Bundibugyo vaccine trial begins in Uganda

trackers.title: Mpox Tracker: Africa & World
trackers.description: Independent, sourced mpox tracker: WHO case counts for Africa, countries with active transmission, clade Ib spread in Europe and the US, vaccines, emergency status and a dated timeline.

status.label: Active · no global emergency
status.summary: WHO ended its global mpox emergency in September 2025, and Africa CDC lifted its continental emergency on 22 January 2026, but cases continue. WHO counted 1,153 confirmed cases and 7 deaths in 11 African countries in the six weeks to 16 August, 785 of them in Madagascar, where a clade Ib outbreak that began in December 2025 has passed 3,000 confirmed cases. Outside Africa, clade Ib is spreading locally in Europe, mostly among men who have sex with men, and CDC says sustained spread in the US is likely.

trackers.headline: WHO counted 1,153 confirmed mpox cases in 11 African countries in the six weeks to 16 August, most in Madagascar. CDC says sustained clade Ib spread in the US is likely.

trackers.title: Cholera Tracker: Global
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of cholera worldwide in 2026: WHO case and death counts, countries reporting cases, how this year compares with 2025, WHO's risk level and a dated timeline.

status.label: Slowing · below 2025's pace
status.summary: WHO counted 275,284 cholera and acute watery diarrhoea cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries from 1 January to 30 August, 43% fewer cases and 58% fewer deaths than a year earlier, and August's cases fell 25% from July. Afghanistan, Nigeria and DR Congo report the most cases. WHO rated the global risk very high in June, and 2025 brought the most cholera deaths reported to WHO since 1999.

trackers.headline: WHO counts 275,284 cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries by 30 August, 43% fewer cases than a year earlier. 2025 had the most deaths since 1999.

latest.title: WHO: 275,284 cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries
WHO: 2025 had the most cholera deaths since 1999

trackers.title: Dengue Tracker: Europe
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of locally acquired dengue in Europe in 2026: ECDC and national case counts, affected countries and clusters, the yearly trend since 2010, vaccines and a dated timeline.

status.label: Active · new local cases in Italy
status.summary: Italy and France are the only EU/EEA countries with locally acquired dengue this year. Italy's national health institute (ISS) counted 68 local cases in 5 outbreaks by 6 October, in places including the provinces of Livorno, Lecce and Milan and a cluster in Cartigliano (Vicenza) that had reached 8 cases by 2 October; Italy's National Blood Centre added Rome to its list of affected areas on 2 October. France counts 6 cases in 4 episodes. The total is well below the 2024 record of 304. ECDC reports weekly until November.

trackers.headline: Italy has 68 locally acquired dengue cases this year and France 6, well below the 2024 record of 304.

latest.title: Italy: 68 local dengue cases in 5 outbreaks; France unchanged at 6
Cartigliano cluster reaches 8 cases; Rome added to affected areas

trackers.title: Russia Plague Watch
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the suspected plague case in Irkutsk, Siberia: live incubation countdown, case counts, WHO risk level, claim check and a dated timeline.

status.label: Suspected, unconfirmed
status.summary: A 28-year-old worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died overnight on 1–2 October after severe pneumonia. Media reports link the death to pneumonic plague. Russian authorities list the cause as "pneumonia of unknown etiology". On 6 October Russia told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested. On 7 October WHO said it was still waiting for Russia to identify the pathogen and could not yet complete a full risk assessment. On 8 October the regional governor said the hospital quarantine had been lifted and that monitoring of all contacts was complete.

trackers.headline: Russian officials say quarantine at Shelekhov hospital is lifted and monitoring of all contacts is complete. Plague is not confirmed, and WHO is still waiting for Russia to name the pathogen.

latest.title: Governor says quarantine lifted and monitoring of all contacts complete
WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details

trackers.title: Marburg Watch
trackers.description: Independent, sourced Marburg tracker: any new cases in Africa, Uganda's isolated case in 2026, and the full record of Ethiopia's first outbreak (November 2025 to January 2026) with a dated timeline.

status.label: Watching · no new cases reported
status.summary: Uganda notified WHO of a confirmed Marburg case in Kyegegwa district on 30 June 2026: a young child who had died, found through surveillance set up for Ebola. Africa CDC said no contacts had developed symptoms, and no further cases have been reported since. Ethiopia's first outbreak, confirmed in Jinka on 14 November 2025, was declared over on 26 January 2026 after 42 days without a new case. WHO counted 14 confirmed cases, 9 of whom died, plus 5 probable cases who all died. Headlines saying Ethiopia's death toll is climbing date from December 2025.

trackers.headline: No further Marburg cases have been reported since Uganda's isolated case in late June. Ethiopia's first outbreak ended on 26 January with 14 confirmed cases and 9 deaths.

latest.title: Uganda reports a Marburg case in Kyegegwa
WHO reviews its Marburg response in Ethiopia
